svg.text: The buffer, the shift array and the reload control; why a group is 16, 32 or 64 pixels and never 500 ns.
the buffer — sixteen cells, four words deep
the shift path — 16 cells per plane, clocked by the pixel clock
one bit leaves each plane per pixel clock
four of them make the 4-bit index
how four words become pixels — the mode changes the chaining, not the transfer
two chained pairs, 2 bits a pixel
the reload control — both conditions, or no transfer
a 1 per LOAD, cleared after Reload
Miss a reload and sixteen pixels of palette 0 leave the chip: the border colour, for one group — the
"every other 16 pixels background" that demos live with is a transfer that did not happen.
one group in time — four display windows, whichever the mode
Provenance: array geometry and the 4-word transfer from ijor's reverse engineering of the ST Shifter; the reload rule and
the failure mode from the same; the 2 µs grid and the pixels-per-group figures derived in study §4.1. No die geometry claimed.
